html:
Fidel Castro was the Cuban revolutionary who took power in Cuba in 1959 and ruled it for almost fifty years, first as prime minister and then as president until 2008.

A young lawyer, he led a failed attack on the Moncada barracks in 1953 against the dictator Fulgencio Batista. After prison and exile in Mexico, he sailed back in 1956 with a small band that included Che Guevara and his brother Raúl. From the Sierra Maestra mountains they fought a guerrilla war until Batista fled on New Year's Day 1959. This was the Cuban Revolution.

  • He nationalised land and American owned businesses, and the United States cut ties.
  • He beat the US backed Bay of Pigs invasion in 1961 and declared Cuba socialist.
  • He allied with the Soviet Union. Soviet missiles on the island led to the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962, the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.
  • His government spread schooling and health care widely but jailed opponents, banned other parties and saw hundreds of thousands leave for Florida.

He handed power to Raúl in 2008 and died in 2016.
sum: Fidel Castro was the Cuban revolutionary who took power in Cuba in 1959 and ruled it for almost fifty years, first as prime minister and then as president until 2008.
